# Use a native ArkWeb ability with a scoped local-resource origin

## Platform difference

A Flutter launcher can hand a specialized web runtime to an OH-native ability, but the resource origin, script injection and lifecycle become native responsibilities.

## Implementation

Gardendless replaces its Flutter WebView/local-server design with GameAbility and a versioned session. Its resource handler serves a synthetic HTTPS origin, restricts methods/paths and remote hosts, and rejects traversal/symlinks. Follow-up fixes stop a declarative about:blank source from overriding controller navigation, correct the document-start API name and use exact-origin script rules.

## Applicability

This is an optional product architecture for a local web game, not a requirement for ordinary Flutter apps or all WebViews. The launcher-to-game/return path is part of the contract.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A URL glob-looking string may not match the native injection-rule grammar. The inspected path/origin controls are source evidence, not a penetration-test result. A native bridge exposed to arbitrary origins would change the security boundary.

## Verification

Test controller navigation, earliest script access, allowed/disallowed origins, encoded traversal and symlinks, remote requests, ability handoff and return-to-launcher behavior.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
